name: MT48LC16M16A2P-6A:G
title: 256Mb SDR SDRAM, x4, x8 and x16, 3.3 V
summary: A 256 Mbit single-data-rate synchronous DRAM with four internal banks, sold as 64M x 4 (MT48LC64M4A2), 32M x 8 (MT48LC32M8A2) and 16M x 16 (MT48LC16M16A2). Every signal is captured on the rising clock edge; reads and writes are programmable bursts of 1, 2, 4, 8 or a full page, with auto precharge, auto refresh, self refresh and power-down. It runs from 3.3 V ±0.3 V with LVTTL I/O, up to 167 MHz at CL = 3 in the -6A grade, and meets PC100 and PC133. MT48LC16M16A2P-6A:G is the x16 die revision G in the Pb-free 54-pin TSOP II.
key_figures: 3 mA max, 1.5 mA max low power (rev G)

notes: A full order code is base part number, then speed grade (-6A, -75, -7E), then optional L (low-power self refresh) and IT or AT (temperature), then :D or :G for the die revision.
MT48LC16M16A2P-6A:G: 16 Meg x 16, tWR = 2 CLK, 54-pin TSOP II Pb-free, 6 ns cycle at CL = 3 (167 MHz), commercial 0 °C to +70 °C, revision G.
-6A is offered on x8 and x16 only. FG, BG and -75 belong to revision D; F4 and B4 (54-ball 8 x 8 mm VFBGA) to revision G.
FBGA top marks are decoded with the Micron FBGA device decoder at www.micron.com/decoder.

operation.text: A 268,435,456-bit synchronous DRAM split into four banks of 67,108,864 bits. Each bank has 8192 rows; a row holds 2048 columns of 4 bits (x4), 1024 of 8 bits (x8) or 512 of 16 bits (x16). All inputs are captured on the rising CLK edge. The pipeline lets the column address change every clock, and work in one bank can overlap precharge in another so precharge time is hidden.
ACTIVE carries the bank on BA[1:0] and the row on A[12:0]. READ or WRITE carries the first column of the burst: A[9:0] and A11 on x4, A[9:0] on x8, A[8:0] on x16, with A10 choosing auto precharge.

One 3.3 V ±0.3 V supply feeds VDD and VDDQ. They come up together, stay within 300 mV of each other, and VDDQ never exceeds VDD; VSS and VSSQ are at the same potential. Inputs and outputs are LVTTL levels.

Power VDD and VDDQ together, hold CKE LOW and get CLK running within its limits. Wait at least 100 µs, sending only COMMAND INHIBIT or NOP and bringing CKE HIGH during that wait. Then PRECHARGE ALL and wait tRP; issue AUTO REFRESH and wait tRFC, twice (more cycles are allowed). The mode register wakes in an unknown state, so load it with LOAD MODE REGISTER (BA1 = BA0 = 0) and wait tMRD, sending only NOP or DESELECT. The two refreshes may also follow the mode-register load. The outputs are High-Z, guaranteed, from the load onward, and should be High-Z already when it is issued. A12 is LOW when the mode register is loaded.

M[2:0] set burst length, M3 burst type, M[6:4] CAS latency, M[8:7] operating mode (00 only), M9 write burst mode; higher bits are written 0, and BA1, BA0 = 0, 0 select this register. It keeps its value until reloaded or power is lost. Load it only with all banks idle and wait tMRD before the next command; otherwise operation is undefined. Reserved codes are not used.

Bursts of 1, 2, 4 or 8 work with either sequential or interleaved order; a full-page burst exists in sequential order only and, with BURST TERMINATE, gives any length. A burst stays inside an aligned block the size of the burst and wraps at the block edge; the low address bits pick the first column. A full-page burst wraps round the row.
CL, 2 or 3 clocks (1 is also coded), is the delay from READ to data. With READ on edge n, the outputs start driving after edge n + CL - 1 and data is valid at edge n + CL when access times are met.
M9 = 0: the programmed burst length applies to reads and writes. M9 = 1: reads burst as programmed, every write touches a single column.

A row must be opened with ACTIVE before a READ or WRITE to that bank, and READ or WRITE follows after tRCD. A different row in the same bank needs a precharge first; ACTIVE to ACTIVE in one bank is tRC. ACTIVE to another bank may be issued while one is being accessed, spaced by tRRD.

First data appears CL after READ and one word follows on each rising edge; the DQ go High-Z when a burst ends with nothing following. A READ can be issued on any clock after a READ, to the same or another bank, so full-speed random reads are possible; a new READ issued CL - 1 clocks before the last wanted word keeps data continuous. Read data is gated by DQM registered two clocks earlier: HIGH gives High-Z, LOW gives data.

A WRITE can cut off a READ burst, or follow a fixed burst at once, on the clock after the last wanted read data, if bus contention is avoided. DQM is taken HIGH at least two clocks before the WRITE to silence read data; once the WRITE is registered the DQ stay High-Z whatever DQM does, provided DQM was HIGH on the clock just before it. DQM is LOW for the write data itself (zero-clock latency on inputs). At some clock rates a NOP cycle is added between the two.

With auto precharge off, a fixed-length or continuous read burst in a bank is ended by a PRECHARGE to that bank placed CL - 1 clocks ahead of the edge carrying the last data word required. The bank then waits tRP before its next command, and some of that time overlaps the final data. Placed this way at the end of a full fixed burst, PRECHARGE equals auto precharge; it occupies a command slot, and it can also shorten a burst.

BURST TERMINATE cuts off the latest READ or WRITE burst when auto precharge is off. For reads it is issued CL - 1 clocks before the last wanted word. For writes the data on the BURST TERMINATE clock is dropped; the last data written is the word one clock earlier.

The first data word is taken on the WRITE clock and one word on each rising edge after it. After a fixed burst the DQ stay High-Z and further input is ignored; a full-page burst wraps round the row until stopped. A WRITE may follow any clock after a WRITE, to the same or another bank. Write data is masked by DQM on the same clock.
A READ cuts off a WRITE burst; input after the READ is ignored and not written. The last word written is the one registered a clock before the READ.

PRECHARGE to the same bank, auto precharge off, is issued tWR after the clock of the last wanted input word. With tCK below 15 ns, DQM masks input on the clock before and the clock of the PRECHARGE. Auto precharge needs at least one clock of tWR to complete, at any frequency. The bank takes no new command until tRP.
PRECHARGE closes the open row in one bank (A10 LOW, bank on BA[1:0]) or in all banks (A10 HIGH, BA don't care). The bank is idle and ready for ACTIVE after tRP.

A10 HIGH on a READ or WRITE closes that row automatically when the burst ends, at the earliest legal point, as if PRECHARGE had been issued then; the bank takes no command until tRP after that. It applies to one command at a time and does not work with full-page bursts, including single-location writes with full-page length.

A burst with auto precharge in bank n may be cut off by a READ or WRITE to bank m. READ cut by READ: bank m data follows CL later and bank n starts precharge when the new READ registers. READ cut by WRITE: DQM two clocks ahead avoids contention; precharge starts when the WRITE registers. WRITE cut by READ or WRITE: the last word written to bank n is the one a clock before the new command, and bank n starts precharge once tWR has run, counted from the registration of the new command.

AUTO REFRESH (like CAS-before-RAS refresh) refreshes one row from an internal counter, so addresses are don't care. All banks are precharged and tRP met first. No executable command may follow until tRFC; NOP or COMMAND INHIBIT fill that time. 8192 refreshes are needed every 64 ms (commercial, industrial) or 16 ms (automotive), either spread evenly or as a burst at tRFC spacing once per period.

Issued like AUTO REFRESH with CKE LOW. The device refreshes itself without CLK; all inputs except CKE are don't care and CKE stays LOW. It stays in self refresh for at least tRAS. To leave, CLK is made stable, CKE goes HIGH and NOPs are issued for tXSR (at least two clocks) while an internal refresh finishes. Afterwards distributed AUTO REFRESH resumes, since both modes share the row counter. Not available on automotive (AT) parts.

CKE registered LOW with NOP or COMMAND INHIBIT and no access running enters power-down: precharge power-down if all banks are idle, active power-down if a row is open. Input and output buffers other than CKE switch off. No refresh happens, so the device stays no longer than the 64 ms refresh period; breaking the refresh requirement can lose data. NOP or COMMAND INHIBIT with CKE HIGH, meeting tCKS, exits.

CKE registered LOW during a column access or burst freezes the internal clock: each rising edge with CKE LOW suspends the next internal edge. Commands and input data on a suspended edge are ignored, output data stays driven and burst counters hold. CKE registered HIGH resumes operation on the next rising edge.

The clock frequency stays constant during access and precharge states (READ, WRITE including tWR, PRECHARGE); CKE may be used to lower the data rate. CLK and CKE move monotonically between VIL and VIH.
AT parts use a 16 ms refresh period, have no self refresh, and run with ambient and case between –40 °C and +105 °C.

The case temperature TC is taken at the centre of the top of the package. Holding TC inside its limit keeps the junction in range; at high ambient, forced air or a heat sink may be needed. Thermal impedance depends on density, package and die design.
Rows should be accessed evenly; a heavy concentration of accesses on one row address can shorten product life.
